lines.en: There are pros and cons to spending my free time with a small child.
Well, this small child.
I specify this because there aren’t many pros when it comes to hanging out with small children like Chinami, and yet I keep doing that for reasons beyond my comprehension.
But Nao is obviously different.

Her inability to speak offers up the rarest form of peace and quiet in that my loneliness is temporarily quelled by her presence, but there is no need to fill the silence with anything other than the sounds of our breathing.
That would be one of the pros.
The biggest con is that I must accept that even the presence of someone like her is enough to quell my loneliness in the first place- whether it be temporary or not.
The fact remains that my existence only exists to begin with because it is tethered to any girl unfortunate enough to lock eyes with me.
On the ride to the mall, I habitually tell myself that nothing will happen.
But another voice that chases the back of our bus incessantly screams the most disgusting of reminders at me the whole way there.
No one would ever know.

We manage to make it to the mall without anyone assuming I’m a kidnapper...and Nao is expectedly shocked to see somewhere as bright and busy as this for what I can only imagine is the first time in her life.
Though, I haven’t ruled out the possibility that this “life” of hers is just getting started, so that might not be all that impressive at the end of the day.
Either way, here we are.
Now, I just have to figure out what I’m supposed to do when it comes to buying her clothes.

Logic would dictate that I take her to a clothing store because that is where clothes are located — but I have no idea what she would want to wear and I’m not about to try my hand at becoming a fashion-designer.
Thankfully, I know someone who likely will.
Unthankfully, I have no idea how I’m going to explain this to her.
: Nao, I know you might be excited to visit the mall for the first time, but-
: Aaaaand she’s off.
: I should have seen that coming.
: Oh, good. You came back.
: I have no idea how I’m supposed to talk to you. Where’s your notebook?
: You left it on the bus, didn’t you?
: Hah...
: Follow me. I know somewhere we can get you more...body-fabric or whatever it was.
: But you’re going to have to be on your best behavior because there’s a girl who works there that I may or may not be dating. It’s complicated. Just don’t do anything that will get me in trouble.
: I’m glad you agree.
: Now, come on. It’s not far from here.
: Hey, great timing! I had a question about something for the Dorm Wars and I was just about to text you.
: Well, that sucks for you because you’re about to have several more pressing questions and completely forget what you originally wanted to ask me.
: What? Why do you say-
: Sensei.
: Hit me. I mentally prepared myself for every question you could possibly ask me on the way over here.
: Have you been keeping this little girl locked in your closet the whole time you’ve known me because you were afraid I’d get jealous of how cute she is?
: I was apparently not mentally prepared for every question you could possibly ask. But also, no. She’s a stray. Let’s just leave it at that.
: Oh, also, I need to buy clothes for her. Preferably at a discounted rate since we’re seeing each other and this place is too pricey for me.
: Is she like...a relative of yours or something?
: Sure, let’s go with that. That’s way easier than anything I’ve thought of and believable.
: Arf!
: Another girl Chinami’s age! And with funny eyes!
: They’re not funny, Chinami. Be nice. This is Sensei’s...relative.
: Hopefully.
: Don’t worry, Papa’s relative! Chinami isn’t a real dog! Chinami just needs to wear the dog helmet when she goes to the mall so she doesn’t get sick. You are in good paws! Arf!
: I think this is the first time she’s ever seen another girl her size. She’s probably just surprised she’s not the smallest person in existence.
: Yeah, I’m sure the giant furry helmet has nothing to do with it.
: What is your name, Papa’s relative? Chinami’s name is Chinami.
: She’s mute, Chinami. That means she can’t-
: Nao-chan? That’s a very pretty name!
: What? How did-
: Nao-chan, do you have a favorite animal? Chinami’s company, Chinami-Corp, is the leading distributor of animals in all of Kumon-mi!
: We started as a giraffe company, but have now expanded to all sorts of safari animals! If you need it, Chinami’s got it! That’s the Chinami-Corp slogan.
: Chinami’s friend Tsukasa came up with it. Tsukasa has lots of money and invited Chinami to live in her mansion! Cool, right?
: Really? Chinami’s never met anyone who likes rhinos so much before! You’re in luck, Nao-chan! Chinami-Corp just got a brand new shipment!
: How...is she understanding her?
: She’s probably just making things up. She’s a kid, they do that. And it’s something you should know if you’re going to be adopting our first daughter behind my back.
: She’s not our daughter, Chika.
: Good, because Chinami already kind of is and I don’t make enough money to be a mother of two. Plus, I’d feel weird asking you to be my sugar daddy at this stage in our relationship.
: Nao-chan, what else do you like? Chinami wants to know about your hobbies!
: You like reading manga? And you’re here today because all you have is a hoodie and your mommy wants you to buy more clothes?
: See? That. That’s exactly why we’re here. And she even knows her name. How?
: Why are you looking at me? It’s not like I know everything about kids just because I take care of one.
: They’re probably just doing that thing kids do where they connect brainwaves and communicate without having to speak.
: They're doing what?
: The thing I just said. You've seriously never realized how kids can just communicate like that?
: No...I’ve never even heard of that before.
: Well, you probably weren’t very popular when you were younger then.
: Chinami, do you want to-
: Oh, okay. See that? I was about to ask her to go help Nao-chan pick out clothes and they’re already ahead of me.
: Chika, can I just leave her here? I have no idea what I’m doing.
: Are you crazy? Absolutely not. I’m not even supposed to be bringing Chinami to work.
: If I turn the store into a giant daycare center, I’ll lose my job quicker than Kirin loses her top during the dorm’s weekly game night.
: The...dorm has a weekly game night?
: You really didn’t know? We’ve been doing it since all of the Kumon-mi Academy girls transferred in.
: What? How have I not encountered this at any point?

: Because I’m just messing around with you, doofus. You really think I’d spend my free time with Kirin? I just wanted to seize a good opportunity to smack talk her since she’s always trying to flirt with you.
: I feel so betrayed. The only way to make this up to me is by taking Nao off my hands so I can wander around and do adult things.
: Come over tonight and I’ll let you do as many adult things as you want.
: Just maybe don’t bring the kid. I’m pretty open in regard to the whole threesome thing, but even I’ve got my limits, you know?
: First off, don’t tempt me with a good time.
: Second, what does it even matter if you put your job in danger? I thought you were quitting this place to go work at the maid cafe?
: Uhh...after the tour thing Uta took me on, I kind of got the feeling I’m not really wanted there.
: That’s just Ami being Ami. I’m sure she’d settle down once you joined the staff.
: Maybe. But I kind of have to be a little careful when it comes to stepping on Ami’s toes so she doesn’t completely hate me once you and I don’t have to hide our relationship anymore.
: Teenage girls are ruthless, Sensei. One wrong move and that girl might chop my head off.

: If you’re really worried about what you’re supposed to do with her, just treat her like Chinami. You watch her all the time and she loves you. I’m sure Nao-chan will be the same way with a little more time.
: Nao is way different from Chinami.
: How? They’re the same age, aren’t they? If they weren’t, their brainwaves wouldn’t be connecting like they clearly are.
: Nao is just...complicated, okay? And it doesn’t help that her mother is literally insane.
: It didn’t help that my mom died and I turned out okay, didn’t I?
: Granted, I was a little older than she is when that happened, but still.
: Just be yourself and everything will be fine. It’s not like she’s yours forever, right?

: Also, who is her mom and why are you keeping so many important figures in your life away from me when you should be subtly introducing me to them without revealing that I’m your little cum dumpster?
: Why are you being so hot today?
: God, I don’t know! I’ve been like this since I woke up and it’s driving me crazy. I just want to fuck my boyfriend and all I keep hearing is-
: Big sis Chika!
: That. That’s what I keep hearing.
: What, Chinami? Do you need something?
: Yes! Chinami needs big sis Chika and Papa to come to the dressing room so we can unveil Nao-chan’s new look!
: Chinami tried to help her choose clothes, but Nao-chan found things she liked all by herself and Chinami was useless! Sad day!
: Also, it’s Nao-chan’s first time ever choosing her own outfit, so nobody laugh! Got it? Even if it’s bad! Which it’s not because Nao-chan did a great job!
: Will you be paying cash or credit, sir?
: Is there an alternate way I could pay?
: God, don’t do this to me today.
: Ladies and gentlemen! Chinami-Corp introduces...
: Nao-chan 2.0!
: Nao-chan is wearing a brand new shirt from our new “shirt” line! The color is blue, which is also the color of the ocean! And the ocean is where fish are!
: Nao-chan is also wearing a blue skirt, a blue belt, and blue shoes! And since Chinami is good when it comes to context clues, she’s deduced that Nao-chan’s favorite color is probably blue as well!
: Well, her modeling poses definitely need a little work. And I’m no fashion designer, but I think a little less blue might be good as well.
: What do you think, Chika? You’re good at this kind of stuff r-
: KYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!!!!!!!!
: OH...MY...GOD! SHE IS ADORABLE!!!
: THE LITTLE POSES! THE WAY HER OUTFIT IS LIKE, TOTALLY HORRIBLE BUT IN A WAY THAT’S MEGA CUTE SINCE YOU KNOW SHE’S TRYING HER BEST!
: I NEED HER! LET ME HAVE HER! I WANT TO DRESS HER UP IN EVERYTHING WE HAVE!
: Did you hear that, Nao-chan? Big sis Chika loves your outfit! You did a really great job!
: Heheh...hehehehe...you’re mine now, Nao-chan...I’ve always wanted a doll...
: Doing okay over there?
: So, umm...
: Remember earlier when I said it was good that Nao-chan wasn’t our daughter since I can’t afford being a mother of two?
: Is it too late to maybe...change my mind about that?
: Pweeeeeeeease, Daddy? I’ll do anything you want...
: Stop just looking at me. You’re making me feel weird.
Ignoring the fact that Chika hasn’t taken her eyes off of Nao since the moment she stepped out of the dressing room, I think things went pretty well.
Nao is clearly proud of herself, Chinami made a new friend, and her clothes were extremely cheap.
So cheap, in fact, that I didn’t even have to pay for them since the only girl working here at the moment is currently caught in a daze and potentially on the brink of becoming a kidnapper.
In fact, I kind of wish she would so I wouldn’t have to spend any more time-
God damn it...I’m starting to like her.
: Do you like your new outfit, Nao?
: Chinami likes it too!
: But she’s really sad she doesn’t know when she’ll see Nao-chan again...
: Really?! Chinami is very excited! She has doubled her friend count in one day! Chinami-Corp is growing!
: Business-oriented as ever, I see.
: It’s just like Bill Gates always says...“Hi! I’m Bill Gates!”
: Well said, Chinami. Now, say goodbye to Nao. Our mission for the day is complete.
: Are you sure you don’t want to stick around for the rest of the day? Maybe longer? Or maybe we could all just go live together and start a big family somewhere in the mountains?
: Nope. Now that the hard part is over, I’m going to take Nao back to her rightful-ish mother and forget this day ever happened.
: I’ll remember this day for the rest of my life.
: How do you like her this much after one meeting?
: Are you blind? Can you see this creature?
: You were totally normal when she walked in.
: Yeah, and then stuff happened. Now, I would kill for her.
: Well, that won’t be happening. Come on, Nao. We’re going home.
: Bye-bye, Papa! Bring Nao-chan over to visit one day! Preferably somewhere Chinami doesn’t have to wear her dog helmet!
: Will do. And to Chika...I’m sorry.
: Oh, crap.
: ...Uh-oh.
: This is, like...totally not good.
: ...Do I even want to ask?
: I think I’m about to get baby fever.
: And I think I’m about to avoid you until it blows over. See you later, you two.
: Wait, Papa! Come back! Chinami wants a little sister and this might be the best chance we get!
: I agree with Nao.
: Then why are you walking away?!?!
Nao and I leave the mall and...
Honestly?
I’m feeling pretty good.
It’s been weirdly entertaining getting to hang out with her and...I think she’s finally managing to win me over.
Like, sure...there’s the issue of her existence being extremely questionable in nature. But I see no harm in just...letting things play out normally for now, right?
